title: Scoreboard With Top-K Totals
statement:
Build a scoreboard for a game where players earn points over time.

  • Scoreboard() creates an empty scoreboard.
  • addScore(playerId, score) adds score points to the player's total. A player who is not on the board yet starts from 0.
  • top(k) returns the sum of the k highest totals on the board.
  • reset(playerId) sets the player's total back to 0. The player is guaranteed to be on the board.

k is never larger than the number of different players added so far; a reset player counts with a total of 0.

Tests are written as a list of operations and their arguments; the first operation creates the board. The expected output has one entry per operation (null where nothing is returned).

examples.why: Points add up: player 2 goes from 15 to 65. After player 1 is reset, the top two are 65 and 30.
After the reset, player 7 starts again from 0, so only the last 3 points count.

constraints: 1 ≤ k ≤ number of players added so far
hints: A hash map from player to total makes addScore and reset O(1). The only real work is top(k).
Sorting all totals on every top call works. Can you avoid ordering the players that are not in the top k at all?
Keep a min-heap of size k while scanning the totals: push each one and pop the smallest when the heap grows past k. The heap ends up holding the k largest.

explain.intuition:
Two of the three operations are bookkeeping: a map from player id to total handles addScore and reset in constant time. Treat a reset as deleting the player: a total of 0 adds nothing to any sum, so it does not change top.

For top(k) you need the k largest values, not a fully sorted list. A min-heap capped at k items keeps exactly the best k seen so far, with the weakest of them on top, ready to be pushed out. That costs O(n log k) instead of O(n log n), which matters when k is small, like a "top 10" panel on a live leaderboard.
steps: Keep scores: a map from player id to total.
addScore: add to the player's total, starting from 0 if absent.
reset: delete the player from the map.
top(k): scan the totals into a min-heap, popping whenever it holds more than k. Return the sum of what remains.
pitfalls: Overwriting the total in addScore instead of adding to it.
Using a max-heap of every total and popping k times without restoring it, which destroys the data for the next call.
Keeping a heap of totals that is updated on every addScore. Old totals stay in the heap and get counted; a lazy or rebuilt structure is needed.

complexity.time: O(1) for addScore and reset, O(n log k) for top

solutions.title: Map plus sort on demand
solutions.idea: Keep totals in a map. For top(k), sort all totals in descending order and add up the first k.
solutions.time: O(1) updates, O(n log n) per top

solutions.title: Map plus a k-sized min-heap
solutions.idea: For top(k), stream the totals through a min-heap that never holds more than k values; what remains are the k largest.
solutions.time: O(1) updates, O(n log k) per top

followups: Make top(k) fast when it is called far more often than addScore. Which ordered structure would you keep?
Return the ids of the top k players with ties broken by the smaller id.
